title: Human genetics implicates a BACH2-NRF2 axis in fetal haemoglobin activation.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the authors' GitHub repo (sankaranlab/BACH2_hbf). Downloaded and parsed its fine-mapping table hbf-META_finemap_20240712_p5e-8.txt: 30,559 variants with PIP (posterior inclusion probability, a fine-mapping model's estimate that a variant is causal); 65 have PIP>0.5 and 489 SNP IDs are duplicated. Parsed EDFig2d_source_data_nonzero-cs.tsv: 74 credible-set variants across 9 loci. Listed the GWAS Catalog directory for the meta-analysis, GCST90860858: one 2.9 GB TSV (not downloaded, over the 50 MB cap). The GWAS Catalog REST API returned 0 studies for PMID 42816612. The repo README lists 8 per-cohort GWAS Catalog accessions, GCST90860858 to GCST90860865.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The figures of 28,279 individuals, 91 conditionally independent signals and 12 regions come from the abstract. The cohort list and the dbGaP accessions for the TOPMed sickle-cell cohorts (phs001514, phs001608) come from the medRxiv preprint (PMC10055601). The Nature full text is paywalled and was not read, so its data availability statement was not seen.

a1_downloadable.note: Per-person fetal haemoglobin (HbF) levels and genotypes sit in controlled-access cohorts: TOPMed through dbGaP (phs001514, phs001608), plus cohorts such as Rotterdam, INTERVAL and the Thai cohort. Only per-variant summary statistics are public (GWAS Catalog, 2.9 GB meta-analysis TSV), and I checked that listing. The dbGaP accessions come from the preprint text.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no per-item measured label at a usable scale. Per-variant effect size (beta) is a column in the summary statistics, but it is an association statistic estimated across people, not a measurement of each variant. Turning it into a causal label requires fine-mapping and linkage-disequilibrium (LD, correlation between nearby variants) handling.

a3_inputs_present.note: Variants come with chromosome, position (hg19/hg38) and alleles, so sequence windows could be pulled from the reference genome. Seen in the fine-map file.

a4_units_stated.note: PIP is a probability from 0 to 1, and beta is in phenotype standard-deviation units according to the column names. The meta-analysis units were not verified in the 2.9 GB file.

a5_enough_rows.note: The only plausible variant-level target is 'causal for HbF': 74 credible-set variants across 9 loci (EDFig2d file), or 65 variants with PIP>0.5 out of 30,559. That is far under the threshold of about 400 for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~2 MB fine-map table; 2.9 GB summary stats if used
a6_fits_laptop.note: The fine-map table is tiny. The full summary statistics could be streamed.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The paper's 91 signals across 12 regions vs 74 credible-set variants across 9 loci in the repo are not directly comparable: COJO conditional signals (from a stepwise conditional-analysis tool) vs fine-mapped credible sets. Not a clear conflict.

a8_label_provenance.note: PIP is the output of a statistical fine-mapping model (SuSiE/FINEMAP) run on these summary statistics plus LD panels, not a physical measurement. Training on it would distil that model.

existing_models.name: Milton et al. ensemble of genetic risk score models for HbF in sickle cell anaemia (Circulation: Cardiovascular Genetics)
existing_models.score_and_split: Per the search snippet, the known HbF loci explain only about 10-12% of HbF variance; the split was not retrieved.

existing_models.name: K-nearest-neighbours HbF% predictor from BCL11A, HBG2/Xmn1 and HBS1L-MYB genotypes (King's College London, ICICT 2021)
existing_models.score_and_split: 87.25% accuracy reported in the abstract snippet; the split was not retrieved.

backbone.name: AlphaGenome (DNA sequence model) could score the variants, but the labelled set is too small for a head

integration.partner_dataset: Blood-cell trait GWAS (BCX2), the Granja 2019 bone-marrow scATAC-seq (single-cell chromatin accessibility) data, and the AlphaGenome variant-effect atlas
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do sequence-model variant-effect scores rank fine-mapped HbF causal variants above their LD-linked neighbours? With 74 variants this is a case study, not an ML project.

controls.positive_control: Known causal variants such as the BCL11A erythroid-enhancer variant and the HBB-locus/HBS1L-MYB variants should get top scores.
controls.negative_control: Non-credible-set variants in LD with them, at matched distances.
controls.external_validation: None at scale. Earlier HbF GWAS cover the same loci.

honest_claim_h3: At best, a sequence model's scores separate 74 statistically fine-mapped HbF variants from their LD neighbours within 9 loci. That is a small benchmark of model outputs, not a predictor trained on measurements.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA sequence around each variant to predict whether it is a likely cause of higher fetal haemoglobin.
plain_idea.train_on: Sequence windows around 30,559 variants near HbF-associated loci; only 74 sit in credible sets (sets of variants likely to hold the causal one), and 65 have a probability of being causal above 0.5.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a variant is likely causal, where the 'truth' is a statistical fine-mapping probability computed from GWAS (genome-wide association study) results, not a lab measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Picking out the causal variants would point gene-editing groups working on sickle cell disease and beta-thalassaemia to new regulatory targets, but the labelled set is too small to learn from.

ml_idea: Rejected. The per-person HbF labels are controlled-access (dbGaP and other cohorts). The public variant-level labels are about 74 fine-mapped variants from a statistical model, too few and not a measurement.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because the project failed Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the credible-set variants with PIP>0.5: 65 of 30,559 (done, so the project is dead).

verdict_reason: Fails A1, A5 and A8. Per-person HbF levels and genotypes are controlled access through dbGaP and the cohorts. What is public is GWAS summary statistics and about 74 fine-mapped variants whose 'causal' label is a statistical model's posterior, not a measurement.
